newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty cool despite foreign entry in bonds.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty cool despite foreign entry in bonds.

text.p: The Polish zloty kept its composure below well-established central bank intervention levels at 2.5 percent from parity despite some $200 million of foreign bids at Wednesday's fixed bond tender, dealers said.
They said many foreigners may have already done their forex transactions so today's foreign investor bond purchases may not have a large effect on the zloty.
"Many foreign investors already have zlotys on accounts so today's foreign entry may not be seen in forex trade," said Malgorzata Sawicka, senior dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.
For most of the day the zloty calmly drifted sideways against the currency basket, but the local unit inched up in late trade to close straddling the 2.5 percent resistance.
Dealers said the zloty's afternoon rise was mainly a reaction to dollar/mark moves and small client orders.
"Players were sitting on long positions and sold currencies at the end of the day, which along with client orders pushed up the zloty in late trade," Handlowy's Sawicka said.
The zloty closed at 2.53/2.49 percent from the parity rate, just up from Tuesday's close at 2.51/2.47 percent.
It was at 3.1565/75 to the dollar, up from 3.1680/90 on Tuesday and at 1.8350/60 to the mark, down from 1.8295/05.

On the money market one-day rates inched up slightly in late trade after the central bank sold 300 million zlotys of its 91-day bills, but dealers said that large cash inflows should keep rates pinned down around 23 percent this week.
Overnight rates closed at 23.0/24.0 percent from opening's 22.60/23.55 and tomorrow/next at 23.0/23.30 from 22.7/23.20.
"There is surplus cash on the market so rates should hold around 23 percent on Thursday," said Piotr Schmidt of PKO SA.
